pins.head: LAY OUT DECALS, THEN BUY VINYL
pins.title: Adhesive Vinyl Roll Yield: Lay Out the Decals Before You Buy
pins.desc: Nest the designs across a 12-inch-wide layout first, leave a margin for weeding, and measure how many inches of roll one batch really uses. Then the roll length tells you how many batches you get, instead of guessing from the label. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Rolls of sage green and cream adhesive vinyl on a gray cutting mat with a metal ruler and a notepad, beside a window with jars of twine on a shelf above.

pins.head: LET A BOOKCASE SPLIT THE ROOM
pins.title: Studio Apartment Layout: A Low Open Bookcase Splits Sleep From Living
pins.desc: In one room the bed is always in view. A low open cube bookcase set at the foot of the bed marks where the sleeping zone ends, holds books from both sides and still lets light through, and a rug anchors the sitting area on the other side. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A studio apartment with a low open cube bookcase beside a teal sofa, a round wooden coffee table on a patterned rug, and a small desk with an orange chair and a lamp by the wall.

pins.head: BUY THE POUCH, KEEP THE JAR
pins.title: Moisturizer Refills: Keep One Jar and Top It Up From a Pouch
pins.desc: A refill pouch usually costs less per ounce than a new jar and takes less room under the sink. Wash and dry the jar between fills, decant a couple of weeks' worth at a time, and note when the pouch runs low so the next one arrives first. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: An open jar of white cream and a white refill pouch on a bathroom counter by a window, with folded towels and a potted succulent on the shelf behind.

pins.head: RAISE THE SCREEN, STORE BELOW
pins.title: Small Home Office: A Monitor Riser Frees the Desk Underneath
pins.desc: Lifting the screen to eye level also opens a shelf's worth of space under it, where a notebook, a charger or a tray of pens can live off the work surface. On a small desk that one change clears most of the clutter. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A wooden desk by a window with a monitor on a wooden riser, a desk lamp, a potted plant and a letter tray, a teal office chair, and a framed abstract print on the wall.

pins.head: TWO SHELVES AROUND THE PIPES
pins.title: Expandable Two-Tier Under-Sink Organizer That Fits Around the Pipes
pins.desc: The drain trap takes the middle of the cabinet, so a fixed shelf rarely fits. An expandable two-tier rack slides to the width that is left beside the pipes and doubles the floor space for sponges, bottles and spare bags. Measure the gap before you buy. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: An open under-sink cabinet with white drain pipes, a two-tier shelf organizer beside them, and a yellow tape measure stretched across the cabinet floor.

pins.head: BASKETS RIDE ABOVE THE TANK
pins.title: Small Bathroom Storage: A Tension-Rod Shelf Over the Toilet Holds Baskets
pins.desc: The wall above the toilet tank is usually empty because renters cannot drill into it. A tension-rod shelf across the alcove holds two light baskets for spare soap and cotton, and comes down without a mark when you move. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A small white-tiled bathroom with a tension-rod shelf holding two woven baskets above the toilet, a white rolling cart with rolled towels beside it, a wooden vanity, and a rust towel on a hook.

pins.head: SCRAPE THE SIDES AS YOU STIR
pins.title: Mix Epoxy Resin With Fewer Bubbles: Scrape the Cup Walls and Stir Slowly
pins.desc: Unmixed resin clings to the cup walls and bottom, and that is where soft, sticky spots come from. Stir slowly with a flat stick, scrape the sides and floor of the cup as you go, and let the mix rest a minute before pouring so bubbles can rise. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A hand stirring clear epoxy resin in a measuring cup with a wooden stick on a black silicone mat, with a heat gun beside it and a window with plants in the background.

pins.head: FOLD SWEATERS INTO THE CUBBIES
pins.title: Tiny Closet: A Hanging Shelf Organizer Holds the Sweaters Off the Rod
pins.desc: Sweaters stretch out on hangers and take up rod space. A fabric shelf organizer that hangs from the same rod holds them folded in stacks, the rod beside it keeps shirts and jackets, and clear shoe boxes on the floor finish the job. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A small closet with a hanging fabric shelf organizer holding folded sweaters, shirts on slim hangers, a storage box on the top shelf, and clear shoe boxes on the floor.

pins.head: COUNT LOADS, NOT OUNCES
pins.title: Laundry Detergent: Compare Liquid, Powder and Pods by Cost per Load
pins.desc: Jugs are sold by ounces, powder by pounds and pods by count, so the shelf price hides the real comparison. Divide each price by the number of loads printed on the package, and check the dose you actually use. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A white detergent jug, a cardboard box of powder with a scoop, and a glass jar of laundry pods on a wooden shelf in front of stacked folded towels.

pins.head: HANG THE BAGS ON A TENSION ROD
pins.title: Renter-Friendly Storage: A Tension Rod Turns an Alcove Into a Bag Rack
pins.desc: A shallow alcove is too narrow for furniture but just right for a tension rod. Tote bags and a jacket hang from it on hangers, woven baskets stack underneath, and a slim cart holds the smaller things. Nothing is screwed into the wall. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: An alcove with a tension rod holding tote bags and a jacket on hangers, two stacked woven baskets and a slim white rolling cart below, a trailing plant on a shelf above, and a hallway beside it.

pins.head: WHOLE BEANS, FEWER REORDERS
pins.title: Whole Bean Medium Roast Coffee in a 30-Ounce Bag for Fewer Reorders
pins.desc: A larger bag of whole beans means fewer reorders, and beans stay fresher than ground coffee if you grind only what you brew. Mark the day you open it on a calendar and you will know how often the next bag needs to come. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: Two kraft paper coffee bags, a small desk calendar, a ceramic mug and scattered coffee beans on a light wooden kitchen counter by a window.

pins.head: RINSE, BLOT, THEN RACK THEM
pins.title: Paint Brush Care: Rinse, Blot and Rack Brushes Before You Clean Up
pins.desc: Acrylic dries in the ferrule first, so the brushes come before the palette. Rinse each one in clean water, blot it on a towel, reshape the tip and set it in the rack; then the jar and towel are ready for next time. Contains affiliate links.
pins.alt: A wooden rack holding paint brushes upright on a worktable beside an empty glass jar, with jars of twine on a shelf by a window.
